pillars.engagement_stem: You are more likely to contribute your time, effort and identity into a group

GrpProsp.name: Group Prospects
GrpProsp.description: How far you feel the group, as it now stands, can pull off the venture it has agreed to take on and not yet finished: a game, project, season or campaign. It is confidence in the group's capability for that venture, its members' skill included: not luck, not your own prospects (OwnProsp), not whether each will do their part (OutResp), not a general sense that the group is strong.
GrpProsp.footnote: A group with goals is formally defined as a team, but the term group is preferred as it removes the implication of a wider organisation and hierarchy.

anchors.10: You feel sure the group, as it stands, can pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks well within its reach.
anchors.1: You feel sure the group, as it stands, cannot pull off what it has set itself; the venture looks beyond it.

GrpProsp.effect_on_other_pillars: GrpProsp's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute. In other words, the goal still remains to be achieved.
GrpProsp.engagement: That is likely to succeed in goals that you believe are worth pursing, or you would not have joined the group in the first place, and that has agreed goals, or otherwise random changes to the group's direction will move outside the model's ability to predict.
GrpProsp.out_of_scope: Random changes to the group's direction without agreed goals.

pre_language.core: A felt sense, before any words, that this band can bring off what it is setting out to do: the chimpanzee weighing the hunting party and feeling the colobus within reach when enough able hunters are present, and out of reach when they are not. Intimates read it from her bearing as the venture starts: settled and forward-leaning, in step with the others, or hesitant and watchful, eyes on the others rather than the task.

GrpProsp.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
GrpProsp.gloss: Felt confidence the group can pull this off

excluded: Generalised group potency: 'overarching group efficiency' and the generic ability to coordinate on any venture ('hunting ANY animal').
Process efficacy: confidence in the group's coordination, communication and cooperation as such ('ability to coordinate effectively').
Outcome forecast ('will achieve'), including fortune: a probability that the goal comes about, from whatever cause.
The rule that achieved goals drop out and 'may not continue to influence your engagement'.
Personal objectives within the group.

OwnProsp.name: Own Prospects
OwnProsp.description: How likely you feel it is that staying in this group will get you what you yourself are after from it: the place, play, pay, skill, advancement or mate you joined for. It is a forecast of what the group will deliver to you, not your own ability, not the group's own venture, and not a tally of what it has given so far, which only feeds it.

anchors.10: You are sure that staying will bring you what you came for; the group's dealings with you keep opening the way to it.
anchors.1: You are sure that staying will bring you nothing you came for; whatever you do here, the way to it stays shut.

OwnProsp.effect_on_other_pillars: You respond to your current assessment of goal achievement likelihood.
OwnProsp.engagement: Where you feel that you are likely to achieve your personal goals, whether or not they are part of the group goals (GrpProsp) or indeed, conflict with them. Presumably if personal and group goals are in conflict, you would prefer to have low levels of GrpProsp however such a condition is out of scope for the model as it indicates deception and potentially sabotage, which is a cognitive rather than an unconscious drive (as the Pillars are contended to be).
OwnProsp.out_of_scope: Personal goals deliberately in conflict with group goals (deception, sabotage).

pre_language.core: The felt yield of staying with this band for her: whether being here keeps bringing her food, a mate, a place or a skill, or keeps bringing her nothing. Its animal form is the forager's reading that a patch is still worth working, and the primate's reading that staying in this troop will or will not yield what staying costs. Intimates read it from whether she settles in and works at her own aims here, or drifts to the edge, looks outward and leaves.

OwnProsp.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
OwnProsp.gloss: Will staying here get me what I want?

excluded: Own ability: self-efficacy or perceived competence, the 'can I do it' reading.
Satisfaction with what the group has delivered so far.
Hope as an emotion, and hope as agency plus pathways thinking.
Positive fantasies: vivid imagining of the desired outcome.
Comparison with outside alternatives: what she could get elsewhere.
Past achievement as evidence: achieved goals counting toward prospects.
Non-monotonic striving: strongest effort at intermediate likelihood.
Disengagement and re-engagement from unattainable goals.

Status.name: Status
Status.description: Your felt rung in the group's settled order of precedence: how far you go first, take the first turn and the first share as a matter of course, and how far you go after others and take what is left. All recognise the order, so it is not fought out each time. The precedence attaches to your place, however you came by it: an office, seniority, the backing of kin or allies, an old contest no one reopens, or credit for what you bring that has settled, over time, into a place others take for granted. It is distinct from the live deference you draw for what you bring now (Prestige), and it is not held in place by present fear (Levelling).

anchors.10: You go first as a matter of course: the first turn, the first share and the best seat are yours without a word said, and no one in the group stands above you.
anchors.1: You go last as a matter of course: you wait your turn and take your share and seat after everyone else, without a word said, and no one in the group stands below you.

Status.effect_on_other_pillars: Your perception of your status can change due to slight changes to a formal remit, or the willingness people are to be compelled. If they do not respect your authority, you would feel lower status, and influence your behaviour.
Status.engagement: Where you feel that you possess formal power within a group, enabling you to utilise the group to achieve your own vision, which aligns the group with your identity. This is why new leaders often revoke measures taken by the preceding.

pre_language.core: Her felt rung in an order all recognise: the others let her pass, eat and settle first and greet her with the calm signals of submission, or she passes, eats and settles after them and greets them so, and neither side has to fight it out each time. Intimates read it from who passes first when paths cross, who eats first, who takes the best spot, and who greets whom. Read with care: beliefs about the bodily signs of rank outrun the measured signs.

edits.was: This Pillar is the seniority you have been awarded within the group. This is the formal power you have to compel others and make decisions on behalf of the group. A small group may not have a rank structure, but it may formally attribute power unequally. Such power is distinct from that gained informally, or Popularity. Yet both may be the product of common consent, such as voting. The difference is the formalisation of the power, rather than being informal and thus needing to be negotiated.
edits.now: This Pillar is your felt place in the group's settled order of rank: how far others defer to you, give way to you and accept your decisions on behalf of the group. The rank may be conferred formally (an office, a title, a vote) or settled informally over time; what matters is that all recognise it and it need not be renegotiated each time. Deference here goes to your place, whatever others think of your skill.
edits.reason: Status covers rank settled formally or informally (H-to-E panel: formal conferred power has no chimpanzee counterpart, while the wordless core is a settled rank order); the Popularity cross-reference dropped and the boundary drawn against IncResp, which the status literature tends to merge with rank.

was.10: All formal power in the group rests with you, and no one can act without your approval.
was.1: You have no formal power in the group and must seek permission to take any action.

now.10: Everyone in the group gives way to you, and no one acts against your decisions.
now.1: You give way to everyone, and your decisions carry no weight unless others approve them.

edits.reason: Anchors follow the description: deference and give-way instead of formal power.

edits.by: Ben approved, 5 Nov 2026, 11.22 am (comparative psychologist's critique, docs/v3/sc-critique/)
edits.why: The present wording confuses the origin of precedence with its basis. Places are often won by skill or contribution, and in primates through kin and allies or through old contests. What makes precedence Status is that it has settled onto the place and is not fought out or held by fear now. The proposed wording from the brief is closer to the literature, but it needs 'present' fear (settled orders often began in force) and the kin and contest origins, or 'however you came by it' is undercut.

sources.source: de Waal, F., 1986, The integration of dominance and social bonding in primates, Quarterly Review of Biology 61: 459-479
sources.claim: Dominance is integrated with bonding through formalisation (unequivocal communication of status) and conditional reassurance; in some species status differences are attenuated and sharing replaces overt competition.

sources.source: Chapais, B., studies of rank acquisition and maintenance with kin support in captive Japanese macaques (1988 onward)
sources.claim: Kin support is central to acquiring matrilineal rank; once acquired, rank among peers held without kin support when subordinates could not form coalitions.

sources.source: Henrich, J., Gil-White, F., 2001, The evolution of prestige: freely conferred deference as a mechanism for enhancing the benefits of cultural transmission, Evolution and Human Behavior 22: 165-196
sources.claim: Prestige is freely conferred deference, distinct from dominance by force or threat of force.

sources.source: Anderson, C., Kilduff, G., 2009, Why do dominant personalities attain influence in face-to-face groups? The competence-signaling effects of trait dominance, JPSP 96: 491-503
sources.claim: Influence in groups is won through behaviour that signals competence, rated as competent even controlling for actual ability.

sources.source: Willer, R., 2009, Groups reward individual sacrifice: the status solution to the collective action problem, American Sociological Review 74
sources.claim: Higher contributors are seen as more group-motivated and given more influence, cooperation and gifts.

sources.source: Magee, J., Galinsky, A., 2008, Social hierarchy: the self-reinforcing nature of power and status, Academy of Management Annals 2: 351-398
sources.claim: Status, as respect in others' eyes, generates expectations favouring those with a prior advantage, so status hierarchies reinforce themselves.

Status.gloss: Your rung in the settled order of precedence

excluded: Others accept your decisions on behalf of the group (decision authority)
Respect and admiration earned by skill or contribution (the esteem component of status)
Rank held by force or fear (dominance)
The clause distinguishing formally conferred rank (office, title, vote) from rank settled informally over time, and the legitimacy of the order

NormExp.name: Normative Expression (norm guarding)
NormExp.description: How strongly it strikes you as wrong when another member breaks from the group's settled ways, in act or by openly pressing to change them. It is felt indignation at a breach, not dislike of the person. Intimates read it from whether you pull the member up: an objection, mockery, a cold shoulder or shutting them out. Your own conformity and your openness to ideas are not part of it.

anchors.10: The smallest departure jars you at once as plainly wrong, and intimates see you pull the member up on the spot: a sharp word, a mocking laugh or a turned back.
anchors.1: A member doing or urging something different leaves you unmoved; nothing in you says it is wrong, and intimates see you let it pass.

NormExp.effect_on_other_pillars: NormExp has a delayed impact because it is assumed that your suppression or welcoming of ideas has already occurred. As with DivsExp, there is no assumption that any opinion has been acted on (although the scenario may play out that way).
NormExp.engagement: Where you feel that you can manage (minimise unwelcome or surprising) change, by using your power to reduce any propensity for others to suggest change. While high NormExp undermines Psychological Safety for others, it makes you personally feel safer.

pre_language.core: The bristle at one of the band doing a thing the wrong way. Its sign is the move to pull them up: a protest cry, a shove, a cold shoulder or exclusion. Two and three year olds already protest a puppet's wrong move (Rakoczy et al. 2008); Ju/'hoansi pull up breaches by criticism and mockery (Wiessner 2005); chimpanzees retaliate for their own losses but do not police third-party breaches (Riedl et al. 2012). Intimates read it from how she meets another's departure: with indignation and a rebuke, or with a shrug. Forager bands show the same bristle turned on upstarts and stingy members; in this model that egalitarian form is carried by DivsExp->Levelling. The face here is the guarding of a ranked group's settled ways.

NormExp.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
NormExp.gloss: Indignation at breaches of the group's settled ways

excluded: Endorsing and defending the status quo yourself: expressing support for the group's settled ways and resisting change as such
Unwillingness to hear other members' suggestions (closed-mindedness; the old 1-anchor's 'listening intently')
Self-other asymmetry: feeling high DivsExp yourself while wanting to control others' DivsExp (only your own suggestions heard)
Feeling safer for enforcing (the 'and feeling safer for it' in the wordless version)
The groupthink framing ('similar to Group Think'; mindguards; pressure as a symptom of a cohesion-driven syndrome)
Negative reciprocity: paying back a wrong done to her (routed to NormExp by the Reciprocity proposal)

edits.why: The strongest human evidence for norm guarding comes from egalitarian foragers, and tightness tracks threat, not hierarchy. The deck placement can stand only if the face is defined as guarding a ranked group's settled ways, and the pre-language should say so instead of borrowing forager evidence for it.

sources.claim: Ju/'hoansi criticise and verbally sanction behaviour that disrupts cohesion and sharing.

sources.source: Gelfand, M., et al., 2011, Differences between tight and loose cultures: a 33-nation study, Science 332: 1100-1104
sources.claim: Tightness of norms tracks ecological and historical threat.

OutResp.name: Outgoing Respect
OutResp.description: How far you feel the other members can be counted on to do their part in the shared work: each carries through what they take on and keeps their word, so you leave work in their hands without checking. It is reliability, not skill (GrpProsp): a willing but clumsy member rates high. It reads their part, not the return on your help (Reciprocity), nor their trust in you.

anchors.10: You leave any part of the work with any member and never check up on it; what they take on gets done and what they say they will do holds.
anchors.1: You check up on, chase and redo others' work, expecting them to shirk, cut corners or go back on their word.

OutResp.effect_on_other_pillars: OutResp's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute.
OutResp.engagement: With competent and trustworthy people because you like being associated with 'winners', you admire and wish to model yourself off them, and they can help you to improve.

pre_language.core: Whether she can turn her back on them at a shared task. One who counts on her fellows leaves the watch, the carry or the young in their hands and goes about her own business without looking back; one who does not keeps glancing over, hovers at their work or takes it over herself. Intimates read it from how often she looks back, checks and takes over. The mechanism, trust calibrated to a partner's record, is the one chimpanzees show when they adjust trust to partners who have come through before (Engelmann et al. 2015); what sets this Pillar apart from Reciprocity is what the record is of: the partner's share of a joint task, not a favour returned to her. It is her reading of them; whether they turn their backs on her is a different thing and not read here.

OutResp.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
OutResp.gloss: Others do their part and keep their word

excluded: Competence (the ability facet; others' skill for their roles)
Benevolence (others' good will toward you in particular)
Warmth or sociability (friendliness, likeability)
Her own dependability as the others see it (felt trust: being counted on to deliver)

Levelling.name: Levelling
Levelling.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
Levelling.description: How far you feel no one in the group sets themselves over you: makes you do, drop or endure things by force or fear, or takes more than the group's own reckoning gives them (of shares, credit or say) and makes it stick. Your part rests on going along, not on being made afraid or being shortchanged. It is not rank (Status), acceptance (Belonging), deference for what you bring (Prestige), the return on help (Reciprocity) or the cost of showing yourself (DivsExp). A respected leader, or a settled order you accept, leaves it high; a member you must appease, or one who grabs and gets away with it, lowers it.

anchors.10: No one in the group can make you do or drop anything by force or threat, and no one takes more than their due and keeps it. You move, take your share and go about your business in the strongest member's presence as freely as in anyone's.
anchors.1: One or a few members make you comply through force or fear, or take more than their due and keep it. You watch them warily, fall quiet when they come near, and let them have what they want to head off their anger.

pre_language.core: Freedom from a bully she must appease. The free animal moves, feeds and takes her share in the strongest member's presence without flinching or a glance at that member's mood; the coerced one tracks that member's moods, freezes on approach and does whatever heads off an attack. Intimates read it from whether she watches one particular member warily and shrinks or placates when that member comes near, while staying easy with everyone else.

Levelling.descent: from rank perception, through coalitions of subordinates checking dominants. The capacity to read dominance is turned to levelling it (theory).
Levelling.gloss: No member bends you by force or fear

excluded: Coercion of the others: no one's will runs over the rest (witnessed or group-wide dominance)
Expectation that the others would stand with you against anyone who tried to push you about (coalitional check)
Leader's way rests on the others' going along, never imposed (consent-based legitimacy of leadership)
Appeal to a uniformly egalitarian ancestral band as the ground of the reading

edits.why: Model B has no perception that registers unequal shares or stolen credit, which is the other half of Boehm's egalitarian ethos and the best-known primate fairness finding, and arises often in everyday group life. DivsExp.name: Diverse Expression (felt safety)
DivsExp.description: How safe you feel to show yourself in this group: to let a slip, a mood, a need or a disagreement show, expecting no attack, mockery or rebuff for it. It is your reading of what showing yourself will cost you, not whether you speak up, whether your word carries weight (Prestige), whether you are wanted (Belonging) or whether anyone pushes you about by force or fear (Levelling).

anchors.10: You let slips, moods, needs and disagreements show as they come, expecting no one to pounce on them, laugh at them or turn away.
anchors.1: You scan faces before you move, keep your reactions masked and hold back even a plain need or disagreement, braced for a put-down.

DivsExp.effect_on_other_pillars: DivsExp has a delayed impact because it takes time for your contribution to either heard or ignored. Again, there is no assumption that it has been or will be acted on (although the scenario may play out that way).
DivsExp.engagement: Where you feel that your ideas will be welcomed and well-received. While related to IncResp (HCP), Expression is closer to a norm of Psychological Safety than being given specific respect for one's competence. Such a norm creates a warm, less hostile environment, which is distinct from cohesion: a close, friendly group can still make challenge feel risky.

was.description: This Pillar is what extent your ideas challenging Group Think will be listened to. Not necessarily heeded, although an idea may of course be enacted. Your contribution will involve (or imply) some change to the status quo, such as to authorities, roles, processes, and group goals. DivsExp is related to the norm of Psychological Safety more than to common understanding of freedom to act. Since it relates to a group, no member should be acting unilaterally, or at least outside of their agreed roles and responsibilities. Thus, DivsExp is freedom to suggest change to such constraints. Its reactive core, older than language, is latitude: feeling free to act differently from the group, or to start something new (a new way of doing a task, a new route), without being slapped down. Spoken suggestions are today's chief form of it.

anchors.10: You have absolute confidence that your suggestion for change will be listened to and then considered by the group in a way that respects its complexities and nuances. You feel free to try things differently, and do, without bracing for a slap-down.
anchors.1: You believe that your suggestions will be ignored, or not given due consideration even if (grudgingly) heard. You hold back from doing anything differently, expecting to be slapped down.

pre_language.core: Relaxed against braced among her own: the loose body and open play of an animal that expects no bite from its fellows, against the scanning, self-scratching stillness of one that does (displacement activity rises with social stress: Maestripieri et al. 1992). Intimates read it from how loose or tight she is when eyes turn to her, and from whether she hides a hurt or a want.

Reciprocity.name: Reciprocity
Reciprocity.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
Reciprocity.description: Your felt reading of whether help in this group comes back: what you give is returned, what you ask for is met. It holds until evidence moves it. It concerns the return on help, not whether others carry their part of shared work (OutResp), whether anyone takes more of a common take than their due (Levelling) or where you stand (Status). The egalitarian face reads the return as coming from the group; the hierarchical face, from the partner helped.

anchors.10: Help goes where it is needed and comes back as a matter of course; you count on the return without a second thought, because it has never failed.
anchors.1: What you give is not returned and what you need goes unmet; you expect nothing back from anyone here.

Reciprocity.mechanics: Effects still assume help received (canon). The former IndRecip cards attach to the egalitarian Pillars and the former DirRecip cards to the hierarchical ones, so no card collides. A culture switch (HCP dominance drift, or its reverse) changes the face without resetting the level.
Reciprocity.effect_on_other_pillars: IndRecip's impact on other Pillars is based upon the assumption that assistance has been received. As such, it moves forward in time to the help having been rendered. The provision of assistance is not modelled because its impacts are less predictable. There is no Force card drawn if the character has provided assistance.

E.label: Return from the group
E.description: Help goes to whoever needs it, and the return comes from the group, not from the one helped. It is conditional on membership and standing, not on a tally: a known sharer is given to, a known hoarder is passed over, and whoever has a surplus is pressed to share on demand. Your reading is whether the group pays back what you put into it.

anchors.10: Whoever has gives to whoever needs; what you have put in comes back from any member, and you are pressed to share as one of us.
anchors.1: Giving goes into a hole: nothing comes back from anyone, those with a surplus hide it, and need goes unmet.

pre_language.core: Food handed over on demand within the band, with the return coming from whoever next has a surplus; those who hide food lose standing and are passed over. Intimates read it as a sign in her behaviour: whether she hands her surplus to anyone who asks and asks anyone who has, or holds back from both.

E.engagement: Where you feel that the norm of IndRecip is strong because the group can adapt to challenges smoothly by moving effort to where it is most urgently needed, without needing to debate or cajole, and there is joy in feeling part of collective endeavour where no one prioritises self-interest or their own immediate tasking.

H.label: Return from the partner
H.description: Help flows between particular partners who return it to each other. It is conditional on a return from the same partner: in kind between equals, or across rank, as favour and protection passed down for loyalty and service passed up. Your reading is whether your partners pay you back, not where you stand (Status) or whether they do their part of the shared work (OutResp).

anchors.10: Every partner you help pays you back and those you ask deliver; your patron covers you and your people back you, each in turn.
anchors.1: Partners take and do not return; no one above covers you and no one below backs you; you expect no return from anyone you deal with.

pre_language.core: Grooming returned by the one groomed and support in fights traded between the same two (Schino and Aureli 2008; Schino 2007), with asymmetric exchange across rank: tolerance and protection down, support and deference up. Intimates read it as a sign in her behaviour: whether she keeps giving to those who gave to her and turns from those who did not.

H.engagement: Where you feel that the norm of DirRecip is strong because the group can adapt to challenges smoothly by moving effort to where it is most urgently needed, by trusting each other's word (assuming there are favours that each can do for each other); there is joy in feeling part of an endeavour where promises to return favours are always kept, and your efforts end up being recognised and returned; this version of trust is more honouring a deal, rather than being trusted to carry out tasks reliably (as per IncResp and OutResp).

pre_language.core: The felt return on sharing: grooming that is returned by those groomed (Schino and Aureli 2008) and forager food handed over on demand that comes back from the band's next kill (Peterson 1993). Intimates read it as a sign in her behaviour: whether she hands over on request and asks as of right, expecting the return, or hesitates, hoards and goes without rather than ask.

excluded: Her own readiness to give help (helping behaviour, positive-reciprocity disposition)
Her own readiness to seek help
Negative reciprocity (returning harm for harm)
Costs of helping and of offering (distraction from own tasks, risk of rejection)
The canon that a culture is dominated by one face and not both, and the mapping of unconditional help to egalitarian and conditional help to hierarchical cultures
Evolutionary claims: that unconditional reciprocity distinguishes human from primate collaboration, that direct reciprocity is more common in primates, and that bonobos trade sex for favours
The word unconditional for the egalitarian face
Others' reliability in shared work (doing their part, keeping their word)

Belonging.name: Belonging
Belonging.status: Tightened by the literature 3 Nov 2026 (docs/model-edits/tighten/); provisional
Belonging.description: How far you feel the others want you among them: whether they make room for you and draw you in, or leave you at the edge. It is their acceptance of you, read from how they treat you, not whether they defer to you for skill or contribution (Prestige) or where you stand in the order (Status). The culture's face sets what the acceptance rests on.

anchors.10: Others make room for you on sight and draw you into whatever is going on; you never doubt that you are wanted here.
anchors.1: Gatherings form without you and you are left at the edge; you doubt that anyone wants you here.

Belonging.effect_on_other_pillars: Popularity's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute.

E.label: Wanted as one of their own in good standing
E.description: The others want you among them as one of their own in good standing: you pull with the group and are no burden on it. The acceptance does not rise or fall with your output or with any place in an order, but it is not unconditional: a member who shirks, cheats or feeds on the others is edged out. You read liking from the group as a whole.

anchors.10: Others make room for you and draw you in as a matter of course, and have done so through good seasons and bad; nothing short of your turning against the group would change it.
anchors.1: Gatherings form without you and you are left at the edge: they treat you as a burden or an outsider, not as one of their own.

pre_language.core: Let into the huddle after a failed hunt as readily as after a good one, so long as she still pulls with the band; the one who shirks, cheats or feeds on the others is edged out, however able.

E.engagement: Where you feel comfortable and accepted by the group members, who 'have your back' and will support you in the event of any difficulties, and where you enjoy the power of influence (informal leadership).

H.label: Included while you keep your place
H.description: The others keep you among them so long as you keep to what your place in the order calls for, high or low, and do not step out of line. The acceptance is real but conditional on keeping the place, not on the place itself (Status). You read it from how they treat you while you keep it and from the standing threat of being dropped.

anchors.10: You have kept your place and the others keep you among them: at every gathering a place is made for you, whether high or low, as a matter of course.
anchors.1: You have stepped out of line and been dropped, or were never given a place at all: gatherings form without you and you are kept at the edge.

pre_language.core: Kept in the group, at whatever rank she holds, for as long as she does what her place calls for; the moment she oversteps, the others turn on her or shut her out, and she feels the edge of that long before it happens.

Belonging.gloss: How far the others want you among them

pre_language.core: Being let into the huddle or kept out of it, time after time. The others shift to make a place, share, groom and turn towards her, or close ranks, turn away and leave her at the fringe, and keep doing so. Intimates read it from whether she moves freely into the middle of the group or hovers at its edge, watching for a gap.

excluded: Uniqueness and authenticity: being valued for what makes you different, and free to be yourself in the group

Being valued for your contribution (perceived value, competence- or contribution-based respect)
Being 'one of us': group identification, solidarity and centrality of membership
Inclusion in decision-making, information and influence networks

Prestige.name: Prestige
Prestige.description: How far you feel the others defer to you freely for what you bring the group: skill, knowledge or contribution it values. They watch how you do it, copy you, bring you problems, take your advice, hand you decisions and jobs that matter and take your word on them. The deference is given, not owed to any place in a rank order (Status). Being handed a decision or a job because of what you bring is part of it; whether the others think you will carry your share of the work is not. It fades once what you bring does, unless it has settled into your place (Status).

anchors.10: Whenever your kind of skill or contribution counts, the others turn to you, watch and copy how you do it, bring you their problems and take your advice.
anchors.1: No one asks you, watches you or copies you; when your kind of skill or contribution is needed they turn to someone else.

Prestige.effect_on_other_pillars: You respond to the current assessment of others' respect for you.

pre_language.core: Being the one others watch, copy and seek out: eyes on her hands, bodies drawn near while she works, problems brought to her, her way of doing things taken up, the giver sought as a partner; as children and apes attend to and copy skilled or much-attended models, and as the most giving members of a group are sought out and honoured. Intimates read it from who gets watched, copied and sought, and who is passed over when a task of her kind comes up.

forces.name: Making Fetch Happen
forces.increment_logic: When the others draw me in as one of their own, and after a knock one of them comes and sits with me, my bracing eases; I expect a slip, a mood or a disagreement of mine to be taken as coming from one of their own, and my felt safety to show myself rises.

pre_language.decrement: When others leave her at the edge, she watches faces, masks her reactions and braces for a snap.

reactive_test.reason: Felt acceptance relaxing or tightening the guard on oneself is an immediate emotional reaction with a clear pre-language form.

forces.name: Open or masked
forces.explanation: Whether feeling safe to show myself draws the others closer depends on what I would be showing them. Circumstance one: I pull my share of the work, so what shows is moods, owned slips and disagreements aired for the group's sake. HIGH: I let them show, the others read me as one of their own and draw me in, so my Belonging rises. LOW: braced and masked, I come across as aloof even while I pull my share, and they leave me at the edge of the talk, so my Belonging falls. Circumstance two: what I have to show is mostly a run of needs and complaints the others would have to carry, and they have begun to tire of carrying them. HIGH: I go on letting them show, I read more and more as a burden and they edge away, so my Belonging falls. LOW: braced and masked, I keep those needs to myself; with nothing new to carry, they stop edging away and let me back into the talk, so my Belonging rises. Someone already wanted among them is borne with longer. Masked expression lowers a partner's rapport and wish to affiliate (Butler et al. 2003), and disclosure draws liking (Collins and Miller 1994), for circumstance one.

pre_language.explanation: When she does her share alongside the others, showing her moods and fumbles freely draws them to her, while going still and masked leaves her on the edge. When the others have begun to turn from her constant wants and complaints, showing more of them makes them turn further away, while keeping them hidden lets them come back to her and make room for her again.

reactive_test.reason: Both directions are others' felt reactions to what she shows, read by her as warmth or coldness, with no worked-out plan involved.

forces.explanation: Her own investment carries a feeling (enthusiasm or flatness), and that feeling seeps unbidden into her reading of the group's capability for the venture still ahead. The Affect Infusion Model describes the route: mood colours judgements she builds from scratch, whether by quick heuristics or by working them through, and colours least those she simply recalls or makes with a set aim in view (Forgas 1995). forces.explanation: In forager bands, the absence of a bully rests on a levelling coalition of the rest, ready to check a would-be dominant (Boehm 1993). When it is low nothing here seems worth a stand, and the same forcefulness feels like a threat she must appease. Whether the others would back her is a separate matter, carried by Friends at my back (Belonging). Levelling here is her own felt exposure to force or fear, and leaves aside whether she likes or rates the forceful member.

forces.explanation: A change in the venture's prospects changes how much seems to hang on each member's showing; the circumstance that sets the direction on the low side is whether this group meets trouble by looking at what to change or at who is at fault. Circumstance one, the group looks at what to change. forces.increment_logic: When I feel sure the group can pull off the venture, I see no call for anyone to take charge by force or settle things over our heads, and if the strongest starts to drive the pace the rest of us shrug it off; I go about my business beside them without a glance at their mood: my sense that no one here can set themselves over me rises.

forces.explanation: Under threat of failure, groups centralise control and accept forceful direction (threat rigidity: Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981), and would-be dominants meet less resistance. When people feel a loss of control under uncertainty they turn towards dominant rather than prestigious leaders (Kakkar and Sivanathan 2017, over 140,000 participants in 69 countries), so a failing venture lends a would-be dominant the support that would otherwise check him. On the high side, members confident of success see no need for anyone to take charge, so a would-be dominant who tries to drive the pace is shrugged off. Direction that rests on force, or that settles things without a hearing, lowers a member's Levelling; a respected leader simply taking the lead would not. The increment should be modest.

forces.name: Putting in, looked to
forces.increment_logic: When I have just put more of myself into the group, what I brought to that scene seems to show: I feel the others turning to me, watching how I do it and taking my advice, and my sense that they defer to me for what I bring rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I have just pulled back from the group, I brought little to that scene, and I feel the others look past me to someone else when it counts; my sense that they defer to me for what I bring falls.
forces.explanation: Prestige is deference freely conferred on those whose skill or contribution others value (Henrich and Gil-White 2001), and members who contribute more to the group are seen as more group-motivated and given more influence and deference (Willer 2009; Hardy and Van Vugt 2006). The reading is an inference from ambiguous cues, and her own recent conduct colours it: having just put in more, she sees herself as one who contributes (self-perception) and reads others' questions and glances as turning to her; having just pulled back, she reads their turning elsewhere as her contribution no longer counting. Moderate confidence.

forces.name: The long shadow of staying
forces.increment_logic: When I am putting much of myself into the group and mean to stay, I feel we will be around each other long enough for every favour to come back, and I read what I give my partners as sure to be repaid; my sense that help I give comes back from those I help rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I am putting little of myself into the group and am half out of the door, I feel I may not be around when a favour falls due, and I read my partners as having no reason to repay one who is leaving; my sense that help I give comes back from those I help falls.
forces.explanation: Conditional exchange holds only while partners expect to meet again: the shadow of the future (Axelrod 1984). In the lab, cooperation rises with the chance of continued play and falls as the end nears, close to what theory predicts (Dal Bó 2005). Primate grooming and support exchanges run over long periods between stable partners (Schino and Aureli). How long she means to stay is part of Engagement: a member who has put much of herself in sees herself staying, one who is gone or going does not. High Engagement lengthens the felt horizon on both sides, so she reads partners, and a patron across rank, as bound to repay one who stays loyal. Low Engagement shortens it, and she reads herself as the one partners will stop repaying. The partner face applies: what moves is her reading of the return, not her readiness to deal.

pre_language.increment: Settled in the troop, she grooms her partners and feels them groom her back and come to her side in a fight. Her sense that her partners repay her rises.
pre_language.decrement: Half gone from the troop, she feels her partners slow to groom her back or to come to her aid. Her sense that her partners repay her falls.

reactive_test.reason: A felt reading of whether partners will pay back, shaped by her sense of staying or going; no deliberate calculation of returns is required.

forces.name: Giving more, given way to
forces.increment_logic: When this group is part of who I am, I am there at every turn and share and stand on my place; when someone above me hangs back or is away, I step into the turn they leave and the others let me: my felt rung in the order rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I am pulling out of this group, I no longer stand on my place; I hang back and let others take the first turn and the first share, and they go before me as if I were already gone: my felt rung in the order falls.
forces.explanation: Precedence here is owed to place, and a place is held by one who stays in it. Members above and below are always drifting, falling away or leaving, and the turns and shares they stop standing on pass to whoever is there to step into them. A member for whom the group is part of who she is is always there, steps into the precedence others leave, and is let keep it, so over many plays she moves up the order as far as kin, allies and office allow. One who is withdrawing stops standing on her place, hangs back, and is passed over as if already gone, which she feels as her rung slipping. Where rank passes by queue or tenure, staying is itself the route up (social queuing: Kokko and Johnstone 1999; male spotted hyenas: East and Hofer 2001), as seniority is in human organisations. Standing won by contribution routes through H:Prestige->Status; this card covers only holding and taking up place by staying.

pre_language.decrement: Drifting from the troop, she hangs back and others go to the food before her: her felt place in the order falls.

forces.name: Guarding the ways earns a place
forces.explanation: Whether pulling up a breach draws the others round her depends on whether they share the bristle. Circumstance one, the breach falls short of what the group plainly stands for and the others are already muttering (a member skipping the rota the rest keep). HIGH: she pulls the breacher up, the others close ranks with her, and her Belonging rises. LOW: she lets it pass while they bristle, they read her as soft on the ways and cool towards her, and her Belonging falls. Circumstance two, the others do not share the bristle (a small departure, or one that overshoots the group's ideal rather than falling short of it). HIGH: she pulls up a member the others think harmless or even admirable; they read her as a scold setting herself above them and edge away, so her Belonging falls. LOW: she lets it pass with the rest and stays one of them, so her Belonging holds or rises a little. Members derogate anti-norm fellow members and like pro-norm ones (Abrams et al. 2000), so siding with the group against an anti-norm breach aligns her with it. People also put down the morally motivated who seem to reproach them (Minson and Monin 2012). Third-party punishers are trusted (Jordan et al. 2016), but trust is not inclusion. Circumstance one is the default in ranked groups with settled ways.

pre_language.increment: When she bristles and threatens a member trying a new way, others side with her and keep her close, and her sense of being kept in the troop rises.
pre_language.decrement: When she lets a member's new way go unchallenged, others turn from her, and her sense of being kept in the troop sinks.

reactive_test.reason: Indignation at a breach and a felt sense of others closing ranks or cooling are reactions and inferences from emotionally weighted cues, with clear pre-language forms.

forces.name: Pulling up within or beyond place
forces.explanation: Whether a member's indignation at a breach moves her precedence depends on whose breaches come before her. Circumstance one, members ranked below her are breaking the settled ways, pressing in at turns and shares. HIGH: pulling up a junior is what her place allows; the others back her, the juniors who had begun crowding in are put back behind her, and she takes again the first turns they had been taking from her, so her Status rises. LOW: letting juniors' breaches pass lets them edge ahead of her at turns and shares, so her Status falls. Circumstance two, a member ranked above her breaks the settled ways and others at her rung pull that senior up. HIGH: she joins in, oversteps her place with them, and is put back and made to wait her turn, so her Status falls. LOW: the senior's breach leaves her unmoved and she lets it pass, which is what her place calls for; those of her rung who objected are put back, and she now goes before them at turns and shares, so her Status rises.

pre_language.explanation: Whether her bristling at a new way shifts her place depends on who it came from. When lower-ranked members start pushing in at the food, snapping at them sends them back and she eats before them again, while letting them be sees them push ahead of her. When a higher-ranked one does something new and others of her standing snap at it, snapping with them gets her threatened back and made to wait until the others have eaten, while keeping still sees those who snapped pushed back and her going to the food before them.

reactive_test.reason: Indignation at a breach and the felt rise or fall in precedence that follows from how others respond are reactions with direct primate analogues, not a worked-out course of action.

forces.explanation: Hope drives her to approach and pursue, and its absence lets her drift; whether the ranked group keeps her close depends on whether her aims lie within what her rank allows. forces.name: Comfortable in my Own Skin
forces.increment_logic: When no one turns to me, watches or copies me any more, my footing feels hollow, and another member's break from the settled ways jars me as wrong: I bristle and pull them up, and my sense that such a breach is plainly wrong rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When the others turn to me, copy how I do things and bring me their problems, my footing feels earned, and another member's break from the settled ways jars me less: I am readier to let it pass, and my sense that such a breach is wrong falls.
forces.explanation: The mechanism is threat and rigidity. Feeling that no one defers to her for what she brings is a threat to her worth in the group. Under threat, people narrow their attention and tighten control (Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981). Self-uncertainty draws people to clear, rigid norms and sharpens their reaction to deviants (Hogg's uncertainty-identity theory). Threats to self-image raise derogation of others, and self-affirmation removes it (Fein and Spencer 1997); when a person's felt competence is threatened, she turns on others in hostile ways (Fast and Chen 2009, where affirming self-worth removed the effect). The settled ways are ground on which her place is still secure, so another member's breach jars as a further threat and strikes her as wrong: NormExp rises. When others defer to her for what she brings, the threat lifts and a breach jars less: NormExp falls. The evidence shows the threat adding indignation and affirmation taking that addition away, so the fall should be smaller than the rise. The card follows a single source level. Her own conformity and her openness to new ideas are not NormExp and are left to other Pillars' cards. Fast and Chen's finding concerns power-holders whose competence is in doubt, so the effect is strongest where Status is high and Prestige low, and modest otherwise.

pre_language.decrement: When others watch and copy her and bring their troubles to her, she is loose and unthreatened, and lets a member who starts a new way go on unchallenged; her guarding of the settled ways eases.

forces.name: Rank draws the circle
forces.increment_logic: When I go first as a matter of course and take the first share and the best seat, the others cluster round me and I feel no threat of being dropped: my sense of being kept among them in my place rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I go last and take what is left, I feel how little slack my place gives me and that any step out of line would see me dropped: my sense of being kept among them falls.
forces.explanation: In ranked groups, attention and affiliation flow up the order: high-ranked members are groomed, approached and kept central (Seyfarth 1977). Under this deck's face a place is made for members high or low who keep to it, so rank does not decide inclusion outright; what moves is the felt threat of being dropped. A member who goes first feels her keeping is beyond question; one who goes last feels how little slack her place gives her, and that any step out of line would see her dropped. A member settled at the bottom who keeps to her place may still feel fairly secure, so the fall there is modest. Anxiety about exclusion among middle-status members (Phillips and Zuckerman 2001) cannot be carried by a card that follows a single source level and is left to play.

forces.name: Self Interest Quo
forces.increment_logic: Secure at the top of the order, I feel a member's break from the settled ways as a break in the order that puts me first; it jars at once and I pull them up: my sense that such a breach is plainly wrong rises.
forces.decrement_logic: Low in the order, the settled ways are what keep me last, so a member breaking from them stirs nothing in me and I let it pass: my sense that such a breach is wrong falls.
forces.explanation: Proposal, modest weight. Those an order puts first have most to lose by a breach of it, so a breach of the settled ways jars them as a breach of their own place; those it holds at the bottom have less stake. The indignation is felt, not reasoned. Social dominance theory, which the card used to rest on, concerns attitudes to rank between social groups and is a trait measure, so it is set aside. The nearest checked evidence warns against a steep slope: members in the middle of an order, not the top, are least likely to risk their acceptance (Phillips and Zuckerman 2001), and the top is often given latitude (Hollander). That evidence concerns members' own conformity, not their reaction to others, so it bounds this card rather than replacing it. Some low-ranked members also defend the order that holds them down (system justification), so the decrement is small. The card follows a single source level and cannot carry a middle peak; H:Belonging->NormExp (place on trial) carries the insecure middle. Only her reaction to others' breaches moves here.

pre_language.decrement: Low in the order, she watches another member do something in a new way and lets it pass, unbothered.

forces.name: Faltering venture tightens ranks
forces.increment_logic: When I feel sure the group as it stands cannot pull off what it has set itself, a member doing things differently or pressing to change our ways jars me as wrong and I am quick to pull them up: my indignation at breaches rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When the venture looks well within our reach, a member trying something different or urging a change leaves me unmoved and I let it pass: my indignation at breaches eases.
forces.explanation: A felt threat to the group's venture narrows attention onto the established way of doing things and makes departures from it feel dangerous, so indignation at breaches rises; when success looks secure there is slack, and departures are tolerated. The most direct small-group evidence: in freely interacting groups, an opinion deviate was rejected more when the dissent came close to the group's decision deadline, when members' need for closure was high (Kruglanski and Webster 1991). Under threat, control constricts (Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981). The card covers the acute, felt jar of a faltering venture. A slow failure the group has openly acknowledged can work the other way, opening members to calls for change (problemistic search: Cyert and March), and Gelfand's tightness evidence comes mainly from societies over long spans. The effect should therefore be modest.

pre_language.increment: When the band's venture is going badly and the prize looks out of reach, she clings to the usual way of doing it and bristles at a fellow who does it differently, with a protest or a shove. Her norm guarding rises.
pre_language.decrement: When the prize looks well within the band's reach, she lets a fellow try an odd way of doing it without a second look. Her bristle at breaches subsides.

reactive_test.reason: Narrowed attention and a pull back to familiar routines under threat are unbidden and have animal analogues, but the step from that rigidity to indignation at others' departures is shown mainly at organisational and societal scale, and chimpanzees do not police third-party breaches, so the pre-language analogue is weaker than for the other two cards.

forces.framework: Need for closure and rejection of deviates (Kruglanski and Webster 1991); threat rigidity (Staw, Sandelands and Dutton 1981); uncertainty-identity theory (Hogg).

forces.name: Shirkers sharpen the bristle
forces.increment_logic: When I keep having to check up on, chase and redo what others took on, the next member who departs from the way we do the shared work jars me at once as plainly wrong, as if it were one more corner cut, and I pull them up with a sharp word or a turned back: my indignation at breaches rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I can leave any part of the work with any member, a member doing the shared work their own way strikes me as harmless, coming from people who deliver, and I let it pass: my indignation at breaches eases.
forces.explanation: Anger at free riders drives costly punishment of them (Fehr and Gächter). The evidence concerns breaches of the cooperative task rather than any departure from the group's ways, so the card is limited to the way the shared work is done: where shirking is rife, a different way of doing the work is read as another dodge. A record of delivery earns latitude (Hollander's idiosyncrasy credit). Hollander's credit belongs to each member's own record, so carrying it over to the group's reliability as a whole is an approximation.

pre_language.increment: When the others keep leaving their end of the carry or the watch to her, she bristles sooner at any of them doing a thing the wrong way and moves to pull them up: a protest cry, a shove, a cold shoulder. Her norm guarding rises.
pre_language.decrement: When the others reliably hold their end of the shared task, she meets a fellow's odd way of doing things with a shrug and goes about her business. Her bristle at breaches subsides.

reactive_test.reason: Anger at those who leave her the work is an unbidden emotional reaction with a clear primate analogue in retaliation for one's own losses; the generalisation to third-party breaches is human-specific but already present in toddlers' protest, and the card moves felt indignation, not a planned sanctioning strategy. forces.increment_logic: When I go first as a matter of course, what I put forward is listened to before it has shown its worth: the others take up my suggestion, bring me the next problem and credit me with the result, and I feel them turn to me for what I bring: my sense that they defer to me for it rises.

forces.name: Settling into a place
forces.increment_logic: When the others keep turning to me for what I bring, hand me decisions and leave jobs that matter in my hands, they come to wait for me and give me the first word as a matter of course, and I feel it has become my place: my felt rung in the order rises.

forces.explanation: Freely conferred deference is a route to rank (Henrich and Gil-White; Cheng et al.). Contributors are repaid with standing and influence (Willer), and perceived competence buys influence (Anderson and Kilduff). forces.name: Backed into my place
forces.increment_logic: When I am kept among them and my allies stay close, a challenge to my turn or my share brings them to my side, the challenger gives way, and I take the turns that were in doubt: my felt rung in the order rises.

forces.explanation: In macaques, kin and allied support is central to acquiring rank (Chapais), and grooming is traded for agonistic support (Schino), with grooming directed up the hierarchy for rank-related benefits (Seyfarth; Schino and Aureli). So in a settled order she accepts, a low place moves Levelling little, as Model B's own Levelling text says; the card bites when someone uses her low place to push or take. Set it small in settled orders and larger in despotic ones.

forces.name: Ideas aired, ideas taken up
forces.increment_logic: When I feel safe to let a disagreement or a half-formed idea show, I put forward how we might do the work better in front of the others; they take it up, bring me the next problem of that kind and look to me when it comes round again: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When I brace and keep my ideas masked, what I could bring stays in my head; the others never see it, take the next problem to whoever spoke up, and I watch my kind of skill go to them: my sense that they turn to me for what I bring falls.
forces.explanation: Speaking up raises the status colleagues confer, partly because those who speak are seen as more agentic and competent (Weiss and Morrison 2019). Promotive voice, ideas for doing things better, raised peer-rated status and later leader emergence, while prohibitive voice, raising concerns, did not; men gained more than women (McClean et al. 2018). Members who act confidently are judged competent and gain influence even when their answers are no better (Anderson and Kilduff 2009). The card covers ideas offered to improve the shared work; voicing alarm or criticism is not covered and may cost her. Set it smaller for women members. Deck X: DivsExp is egalitarian, Prestige hierarchical. It forms a Reinforce loop with X:Prestige->DivsExp; the brake is a visible failure of what she puts forward (Prestige evidence).

forces.name: No passengers
forces.increment_logic: When every member carries through what they take on, no one is eating from a pot they did not fill, and each share matches what each has put in: my sense that no one here takes more than their due and keeps it rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When some members coast and still take the same share of credit and reward as those who carry them, I see them taking what they have not earned and getting away with it, and I feel a sucker for carrying them: my sense that no one here takes more than their due and keeps it falls.
forces.explanation: Members cut their own effort rather than be the sucker who carries a capable partner who free rides, a reaction to broken equity and reciprocity norms (Kerr 1983). Negative emotion towards free riders drives costly punishment of them (Fehr and Gächter 2002). A free rider who shares the group's take gets more than the group's reckoning gives, which is what Levelling's second limb reads. The card holds where the take is shared; where reward tracks each member's own input, shirking costs the shirker and Levelling is untouched. Modest; forms a Reinforce loop with E:Levelling->OutResp.

forces.name: Credit to spend
forces.increment_logic: When the others turn to me for what I bring and take my advice, I feel a slip of mine would be put down to a bad day rather than held against me, and I let my doubts and disagreements show: my felt safety to show myself rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When no one turns to me any more, I feel every slip would be counted against me with nothing to set against it, so I keep my doubts and disagreements masked: my felt safety to show myself falls.
forces.explanation: Higher status goes with greater felt psychological safety (Nembhard and Edmondson 2006); standing releases approach and expression, while low standing primes attention to threat and inhibition (Keltner, Gruenfeld and Anderson 2003). Hollander's idiosyncrasy credit says members who have earned standing are allowed more latitude, but direct tests are few and weak, so the card rests on the safety and power evidence. X:Status->DivsExp carries the route through settled place; this card carries live deference and should be the weaker of the two.

forces.name: Good season, open hands
forces.increment_logic: When the venture looks well within our reach, I am buoyed, I help whoever asks without counting, and the others do the same around me: my reading that help here comes back rises.
forces.decrement_logic: When the venture looks beyond us, everyone hunches over their own part, help asked for is slow to come and mine goes unreturned: my reading that help here comes back falls.
forces.explanation: Good mood raises helping (Carlson, Charlin and Miller 1988). Mood spreads through a group by contagion, and positive contagion brings more cooperation and less conflict, negative contagion the reverse (Barsade 2002). Confidence in the venture carries that mood, so help flows more freely in a group that expects to win. Under threat, attention narrows (Staw et al. 1981), and each member guards her own part. The step from the group's mood to her felt return is a proposal: common sense, since a winning side is a generous one. Modest; forms a loop with E:Reciprocity->GrpProsp.
